---
title: "Notes"
---

Highlight a few passages on this page and a **N highlights** control appears at the
bottom-left. Open it to see every highlight together, jump between them, remove any, or
export them all as Markdown to paste into your own notes.

The value of a highlight is not the act of marking but the later act of returning. A reader
who marks ten passages in a chapter wants to gather them, not hunt for them by scrolling. An
index turns scattered marks into a small, reviewable set; an export turns that set into
something the reader owns and can carry away.

Because the highlights are stored in the reader's own browser and exported as plain Markdown,
nothing leaves the page to a server. The document stays read-only and authoritative; the
reader keeps a private reading of it that travels by file, not by login. That is the whole
shape of the idea: the author writes once, and each reader owns their reading.

A second paragraph of prose, so there is more than one place to mark. The longer a document,
the more an index earns its keep, since the marks spread out and the scrolling between them
grows. Even on a short page, gathering what you flagged in one list is quietly useful.
